title: Word Search II (Trie + Backtrack)
description: Build a trie of the dictionary, DFS each cell stepping into the trie — early-exit when the next char has no trie edge. Far faster than running Word Search I per word.

notes: Storing the full word at the terminal node avoids reconstructing it from the DFS path.
Set next.word = null after collection — same word reachable from multiple cells would otherwise appear twice.
Mark-and-restore on the board itself is the standard trick to avoid a separate visited set.

questions.q: Why is Trie + DFS better than running Word Search I per word?
options: The trie lets a single DFS test all dictionary prefixes at once and prune dead branches early

questions.q: Why store the FULL word at the terminal node?
options: Avoids rebuilding the word from the DFS path

questions.q: Why set next.word = null after pushing it to results?
options: Dedupes — the same word may be reachable from multiple start cells
Marks visited cells without a separate visited set; restored on backtrack
Required for the trie to work

exercises.prompt: Fill in the trie build and the prune step.

blanks.hint: prune: no trie edge for this character

L3.prompt: Implement findWords(board, words) using a trie + DFS. Run on the standard 4x4 board with words ["oath","pea","eat","rain"] and log the sorted result as a JSON array.
hints: Build the trie once. At each DFS step, look up board[r][c] in the current trie node; if missing, return.
When you hit a terminal (next.word truthy), push and null it out — that dedupes across start cells.
